name: Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant
status_note: Four APR-1400 units (commercial 2021-2024) operate. Spent fuel is held in the reactor pools, which ENEC says can hold 20 to 30 years of discharges; on-site dry cask storage is being studied and a national long-term policy is still being developed.

name: Armenian (Metsamor) nuclear power plant
status_note: Two VVER-440 units; both shut down in 1989 after the Spitak earthquake, and unit 2 restarted in 1995 with operation planned to 2036. Spent fuel is cooled in pools and then moved to an on-site NUHOMS-56V horizontal dry storage facility, which has been expanded in stages.
notes: The operator name has not been confirmed in a primary source.

name: Atucha Nuclear Power Plant (Atucha I and II)
status_note: Atucha I (PHWR, 1974) is in an extended maintenance/life-extension outage and Atucha II (PHWR, 2014) operates. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools (some Atucha I fuel was moved to the Atucha II pools); the ASECQ-I dry storage building at Atucha I (2,844 assemblies) has operated since 2022, and dry storage for Atucha II is being designed.

name: Embalse Nuclear Power Station
status_note: One CANDU-6 unit (commercial 1984) operates after a 2016-2018 life extension and restart in January 2019. Spent fuel spends at least six years in the pool and then goes to the on-site dry storage silos (ASECQ) until a repository is available.

name: Ezeiza Radioactive Waste Management Area (AGE) and FACIRI, Centro Atómico Ezeiza
status_note: CNEA's national radioactive waste management area at the Ezeiza Atomic Centre, with conditioning plant, interim stores for conditioned waste and disused sources, a long-term store for historic waste and the FACIRI store for research reactor spent fuel (217 elements by end of 2018). Former near-surface disposal and semi-containment systems are no longer operated and are under radiological surveillance.

name: Nuclear Engineering Seibersdorf (NES) waste treatment and interim storage
status_note: Austria's only facility for treating, conditioning and storing radioactive waste, on the Seibersdorf research site. Austria produces only low- and intermediate-level waste (no power reactors); storage at NES is contractually secured until 2045, and no decision on final disposal has been taken.
notes: Position of the Seibersdorf research site, on which NES is located.

name: National Radioactive Waste Management Facility, Napandee near Kimba (cancelled)
status_note: Planned national facility for disposal of low-level and storage of intermediate-level waste on about 211 ha at Napandee, about 20 km west of Kimba, declared in November 2021. The Federal Court set the declaration aside on 18 July 2023 for apprehended bias (Barngarla challenge); in August 2023 the government said it would not appeal and would not pursue Napandee or the other shortlisted sites. The Australian Radioactive Waste Agency is looking for alternatives.
notes: Derived position: 20 km west of Kimba town, based on the description of the Napandee property; not a surveyed site coordinate.

name: ANSTO Lucas Heights campus (waste stores and Interim Waste Store)
status_note: Australia's nuclear research campus (OPAL reactor, isotope production) where most of the Commonwealth's low- and intermediate-level waste is stored on site. Two TN-81 casks of intermediate-level residues from reprocessing of Australian research reactor fuel came back from France (2015) and the UK (March 2022) and are kept in the Interim Waste Store until a national facility exists.
operator: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO)

name: Emu Field nuclear test site
status_note: Site of the two British Totem tests in October 1953 (9 and 7 kt, tower shots). Fallout from Totem I drifted across the continent; the site was then considered too contaminated for further tests.
notes: Sources differ on the position: Wikipedia gives -28.634, 132.204, Wikidata -28.698, 132.371; the Wikipedia point is used.

name: Maralinga nuclear test site
status_note: British nuclear tests in 1956 and 1957 (including Operation Antler) and further trials into the early 1960s left plutonium and uranium contamination. After the McClelland Royal Commission, a UK-Australian clean-up buried contaminated soil and debris in trenches about 16 m deep; the land was returned to the Maralinga Tjarutja, though the effectiveness of the clean-up has been disputed.
notes: Sources differ on the clean-up date: completed in 1995 (Wikipedia) or carried out in 1996-2000 (other sources).

name: Montebello Islands nuclear test site
status_note: Three British atmospheric nuclear tests: one in 1952 (Operation Hurricane) and two tower tests in 1956 on Trimouille and Alpha Islands (Mosaic; G2 at 60 kt was the largest explosion in Australia). The islands are now a marine conservation reserve.
notes: Position of the Operation Hurricane test.

name: Ranger uranium mine (rehabilitation)
status_note: Open-pit uranium mine surrounded by Kakadu National Park, operated by ERA from 1980; mining ended in 2012 and processing in January 2021. Tailings have been moved into Pit 3 for capping, and the area must be returned to a state similar to adjacent Kakadu. ERA forecast in 2022 that rehabilitation would finish in late 2027 to late 2028, after the original deadline of January 2026.
notes: The extension of the rehabilitation beyond January 2026 rests on a 2022 legislative amendment; the current schedule is not confirmed.

name: Rum Jungle former uranium mine
status_note: Uranium was mined here from 1954 to 1971 and the site was left unrehabilitated; acid and metal-laden drainage polluted the East Finniss River. After partial works from 1983, Stage 3 rehabilitation (water treatment and rebuilding of waste rock dumps) began in 2022; Phase 3A is funded until the end of 2029.
notes: The 2022 start of Stage 3 is not confirmed in a primary source.

name: Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Unit 1 (VVER-1200) was loaded with 163 fuel assemblies by May 2026 and reached first criticality on 11 October 2026; unit 2 is under construction. No fuel has been discharged yet; under a 2017 agreement spent fuel is to be returned to Russia.
operator: Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd
notes: Status is 'commissioning' because irradiated fuel is so far only in the reactor core, not in the spent fuel pool.

name: Dessel surface disposal facility for short-lived LILW (cAt project)
status_note: Near-surface repository for short-lived low- and intermediate-level waste at Dessel, licensed in 2023. Construction started with the laying of the first stone on 22 September 2025; the first disposal modules are expected to be ready by 2030.
notes: Position of the Belgoprocess site in Dessel, next to which the facility is being built.

name: Belgoprocess waste treatment and storage site, Dessel
status_note: Central Belgian site for treating and storing conditioned radioactive waste: about 300 m3 of high-level waste (mostly vitrified waste returned from reprocessing in France, in buildings 129 and 136), about 4,000 m3 of intermediate-level and about 20,000 m3 of low-level conditioned waste, pending disposal.
notes: The inventory figures are undated. Belgoprocess also runs facilities on a second site in Mol (former Eurochemic reprocessing plant), not covered here.

name: Doel nuclear power station
status_note: Four PWR units (commercial operation 1975-1985); Doel 3 shut down in 2022, Doel 1 and Doel 2 in 2025, Doel 4 remains in operation. Since the 1993 reprocessing moratorium spent fuel has been kept on site in pools and in a dry cask storage building.
notes: A second dry storage building (SF2) has been built; its commissioning date is not confirmed.

name: HADES underground research laboratory, Mol
status_note: Underground research laboratory at 225 m depth in Boom Clay on the SCK CEN site in Mol, built from 1980 and extended 1997-2007, used to study geological disposal of high-level and long-lived waste. It is operated by EURIDICE, a partnership of SCK CEN and ONDRAF/NIRAS.
notes: Position of the SCK CEN site, not the HADES shafts.

name: Tihange nuclear power station
status_note: Three PWR units (commercial operation 1975-1985); Tihange 2 shut down in 2023 and Tihange 1 in 2025, Tihange 3 remains in operation. Spent fuel is stored on site in pools (wet storage); CASTOR casks were contracted in 2016 for storage at Doel and Tihange.
notes: A new dry storage building (SF2) was reportedly completed around 2025; this is not confirmed.

name: Kozloduy nuclear power plant
status_note: Six units: VVER-440 units 1-2 closed at the end of 2002 and 3-4 in 2006; VVER-1000 units 5-6 operate. Spent fuel was sent to Mayak until 1989; it is now kept in reactor pools, an on-site wet store (1990) and a dry spent fuel store opened in May 2011. A LILW treatment and storage facility is also on site.
notes: The nearby Radiana repository for low- and intermediate-level waste is a separate entry.

name: National Disposal Facility for LILW, Radiana site
status_note: Near-surface trench-type repository with reinforced concrete cells for low- and intermediate-level waste, including decommissioning waste from Kozloduy units 1-4. It received its commissioning permit in early April 2026 and was officially opened in mid-April 2026; the first stage has 22 cells for 6,336 containers out of a planned 138,200 m3.
notes: No published coordinates; position estimated from a site description (immediately south of the Kozloduy plant, 3.5 km south-east of Kozloduy town).

name: Permanent Repository for Radioactive Waste Novi Han (SD PRRAW Novi Han)
status_note: Near-surface repository commissioned in October 1962 for institutional waste (never NPP waste), about 7 km from Novi Han near Sofia. Operation was suspended in 1994 for upgrading; the site was modernised with treatment and storage facilities and SE RAW applied for a decommissioning licence in 2025, with waste to be moved to the national repository at Radiana.
notes: Position of Novi Han village; the repository is about 7 km away. Whether the decommissioning licence has been granted is not confirmed; the status reflects the licence application.

name: Abadia de Goiás repository for the Goiânia Cs-137 accident waste (CRCN-CO)
status_note: Final repository near Abadia de Goiás holding about 3,500 m3 (some 6,000 t) of waste from the 1987 Goiânia caesium-137 accident, in drums inside buried engineered structures. It no longer receives waste and is under institutional control and environmental monitoring by CNEN's regional centre CRCN-CO (BR-060, km 174.5).
operator: Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear (CNEN) - Centro Regional de Ciências Nucleares do Centro-Oeste (CRCN-CO)
notes: Position of the Abadia de Goiás municipality; the repository is in the Telma Ortegal state park on the BR-060. 'Low-level' simplifies a mix of contaminated soil, debris and objects.

name: Almirante Alvaro Alberto Nuclear Power Plant (Angra)
status_note: Angra 1 (1985) and Angra 2 (2001) operate; Angra 3 is under construction. Besides the pools, an on-site dry storage facility (UAS, Holtec HI-STORM FW modules, capacity 72 modules) has received fuel since 2021; 30 modules had been loaded by August 2024.

name: Goiânia caesium-137 accident site
status_note: In September 1987 a stolen radiotherapy source (Cs-137, about 50.9 TBq) was opened in Goiânia; four people died and 249 were contaminated. Topsoil and demolished houses were removed and the waste was taken out of the city for storage; about 7 TBq was not recovered and remained dispersed.
notes: 'Closed' means the clean-up is finished and the waste removed; the repository at Abadia de Goiás is a separate entry.

name: Belarusian (Ostrovets/Astravets) nuclear power plant
status_note: Two VVER-1200 units, grid-connected in November 2020 and May 2023. Spent fuel is held at the plant; under the supply agreement it is to be returned to Russia for reprocessing, while the 2023 strategy foresees storing high-level waste at the plant for its lifetime.
notes: Whether any spent fuel has yet been shipped to Russia is not confirmed.

name: Bruce Nuclear Generating Station (Bruce A and B)
status_note: Eight CANDU units (Bruce A and B), several undergoing refurbishment. About 1.48 million used fuel bundles (June 2024) are in the station pools and in dry storage buildings at OPG's Western Waste Management Facility on the Bruce site.
operator: Bruce Power (reactors, leased); Ontario Power Generation (site owner and used fuel dry storage)
notes: Dry storage of Bruce used fuel is part of OPG's Western Waste Management Facility, which has its own entry for low- and intermediate-level waste.

name: Chalk River Laboratories (waste management areas)
status_note: Canada's main nuclear research site since 1944, including the former NRX and NRU reactors (NRU shut down in March 2018 and awaiting decommissioning) and plutonium extraction in the 1950s. It holds legacy waste management areas and stored wastes; a large decommissioning programme is under way and the NSDF is planned on site.
operator: Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (owned by AECL; operated by Nuclear Laboratories Partners of Canada since December 2025)
notes: High-level waste and spent fuel are listed from the site's history of fuel and reprocessing work; no inventory source confirms them.

name: Darlington Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: Four CANDU units, refurbished one at a time (Units 2 and 3 completed 2020 and 2023; Unit 4 due to finish in 2026 per NWMO). About 656,000 used fuel bundles (June 2024) are held in the station pools and in on-site dry storage.

name: Deep geological repository for used nuclear fuel, Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation - Ignace area (Revell site)
status_note: Repository for Canada's used CANDU fuel in the Revell batholith, selected by the NWMO in November 2024 with the support of Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation and the Township of Ignace. A federal impact assessment by review panel is under way (impact statement phase since June 2026); a decision is expected around 2030 and construction from about 2033.
notes: Project point from the federal impact assessment registry; the site itself covers several kilometres.

name: Douglas Point (Waste Facility)
status_note: Prototype 200 MW CANDU reactor operated 1967-1984; its 22,256 used fuel bundles have been in dry storage canisters on site since 1987. Final decommissioning is under way, excluding the reactor building and the spent fuel canister area (after 2030).
operator: Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (for Atomic Energy of Canada Limited)
notes: Located on the Bruce site, next to the Bruce station. The source coordinates appear rounded.

name: Elliot Lake uranium tailings
status_note: Ten former uranium mines (1950s to 1996) around Elliot Lake, Ontario, left about 102 million tons of tailings. All mines were decommissioned between 1992 and 2001; the tailings areas are owned by Rio Algom (BHP) and Denison Mines.
operator: Rio Algom Ltd. and Denison Mines

name: Gentilly site (Gentilly-1 and Gentilly-2)
status_note: Gentilly-2 (CANDU) shut down on 28 December 2012 and is in safe storage; all its used fuel (about 130,000 bundles) is in CANSTOR dry storage modules on site. The adjacent Gentilly-1 prototype (1972-1977/78) is fuel-free since CNL moved its fuel to Chalk River in 2025.
operator: Hydro-Québec (Gentilly-2); Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (Gentilly-1, for AECL)
notes: Sources differ on Gentilly-1: shut down in 1977 (NWMO) or operated intermittently in 1972-1978 (WNN).

name: Kincardine deep geologic repository for low- and intermediate-level waste (cancelled)
status_note: OPG proposed a repository about 680 m beneath the Bruce site for Ontario's low- and intermediate-level waste (application to CNSC 2011). After the Saugeen Ojibway Nation voted 1,058 to 170 against it in January 2020, OPG dropped the Bruce site and said it would seek an alternative.
notes: Shares the Bruce station position; the repository was to sit next to the Western Waste Management Facility. It was never built.

name: Near Surface Disposal Facility (NSDF), Chalk River
status_note: Engineered containment mound for low-level waste on the Chalk River Laboratories site, with a planned operating life of at least 50 years. The CNSC issued a licence to construct on 8 January 2024 (valid to 31 March 2028); a February 2025 Federal Court ruling ordered renewed consultation with Kebaowek First Nation, but the Federal Court of Appeal (2026 FCA 174) set that judgment aside in October 2026, so the approval stands.
notes: Position of the Chalk River Laboratories site, not the facility footprint. A construction licence exists, but physical construction is not confirmed.

name: Nuclear Power Demonstration (NPD), Rolphton
status_note: Canada's first nuclear power reactor, operated 1962-1987; all fuel was removed from the site around 1987-1988 (NWMO lists the NPD bundles in storage at Chalk River). The shut-down plant awaits a decision on in-situ decommissioning.

name: Pickering Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: Eight CANDU units: Units 2 and 3 permanently shut down; NWMO planning assumed Units 1 and 4 would run to end of 2024 and Units 5-8 to end of 2026 before refurbishment. About 864,000 used fuel bundles (June 2024) are held in the station pools and in OPG's on-site Pickering Waste Management Facility dry storage.
notes: Unit shutdown dates after 2024 are planning assumptions (NWMO 2024), not confirmed events.

name: Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: One CANDU unit in operation (refurbished). About 175,000 used fuel bundles (June 2024) are in the spent fuel bay and in above-ground dry storage concrete containers at the station's solid radioactive waste management facility.

name: Port Granby Long-Term Waste Management Facility
status_note: Above-ground engineered mound holding more than 1.3 million tonnes of historic contaminated soil and refinery waste moved away from the Lake Ontario shoreline in south-east Clarington. The mound was capped and closed in autumn 2021 and is now in long-term monitoring.
notes: Position of the historic hamlet of Port Granby, not the mound itself.

name: Port Hope Long-Term Waste Management Facility
status_note: Engineered above-ground mound for about 1.2 million m3 of historic low-level radioactive waste (radium, uranium and thorium residues from former refining) cleaned up in Port Hope under the Port Hope Area Initiative. A June 2026 agreement keeps the facility accepting eligible waste for up to 100 years after closure.
notes: Position of Port Hope; the facility lies south of Highway 401 between Brand Road and Baulch Road. 'NORM' reflects the radium and uranium refining residues.

name: Port Radium (Eldorado mine), Great Bear Lake
status_note: Radium and uranium mine at LaBine Point on Great Bear Lake, worked from the 1930s to 1940 and for uranium from 1942 to 1960, then for silver until 1982. The federal government completed remediation of Port Radium in 2007, removing the remaining infrastructure.

name: Western Waste Management Facility (Bruce site)
status_note: OPG's central store, in operation since 1974 on the Bruce nuclear site near Kincardine, for low- and intermediate-level waste from all Ontario reactors (Bruce, Pickering, Darlington); it also dry-stores Bruce used fuel. Operating licence runs to 31 May 2027 and a renewal is before the CNSC.
notes: Central store for low- and intermediate-level waste from Ontario's whole fleet; the Bruce used fuel dry storage is covered by the Bruce station entry. Position of the Bruce station.

name: Mont Terri Rock Laboratory
status_note: Underground research laboratory in Opalinus Clay near St-Ursanne (canton of Jura), operating since 1996, where international partners study clay rock for geological disposal of radioactive waste. No radioactive waste is stored there.
notes: The operator (swisstopo) is not confirmed in a primary source.

name: Wellenberg (proposed repository for low- and intermediate-level waste)
status_note: Proposed site in Wolfenschiessen (canton of Nidwalden) for a repository for low- and intermediate-level waste in marl. Nidwalden voters rejected the general licence in 1995 and the exploratory tunnel in 2002; the site was briefly re-proposed in 2008 but placed in reserve by Nagra in 2015 and not taken into the final stage of the siting process in 2018.
notes: Planned as a mountain-cavern repository. Formally still a reserve option in the 2018 Federal Council decision, but no project exists since Nördlich Lägern was proposed (2022) for all waste.

name: Beznau nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units (1969 and 1971); Axpo plans to shut down unit 2 in 2032 and unit 1 in 2033. Spent fuel is cooled in the pools and then stored dry in casks in the on-site interim store Zwibez.
notes: Storage of low-level waste in the Zwibez store and its first year of operation are not confirmed in a primary source.

name: Grimsel Test Site
status_note: Underground rock laboratory in the granite of the Aar massif in the Bernese Alps, inaugurated on 20 June 1984. It is not a candidate repository and accepts no waste, but experiments may use radioactive tracers under supervision.
notes: Position of the Juchlistock summit, under which the laboratory lies.

name: Gösgen nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit in operation since 1979. Because pool capacity is limited, the plant runs an on-site independent wet fuel store where spent fuel cools before being sent to the Zwilag central store.

name: Leibstadt nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit in operation since 1984. Spent fuel is held in the plant pools; long-term interim storage is at the Zwilag central store in Würenlingen.
notes: The absence of an on-site dry store is inferred, not stated explicitly in the sources.

name: Mühleberg nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, operated 1972-2019 and being decommissioned by BKW. All 418 spent fuel assemblies were moved to the Zwilag central store in 66 transports, and the plant was declared free of nuclear fuel in September 2023.

name: Nördlich Lägern deep geological repository (planned)
status_note: Planned combined repository for all categories of Swiss radioactive waste in Opalinus Clay, with its surface facility at Haberstal in Stadel (canton of Zürich). Nagra submitted the general licence application on 19 November 2024; a Federal Council decision is expected around 2029, a possible referendum around 2031, and operation from about 2050.
notes: Position of the planned surface facility (Haberstal); the underground layout extends beneath the siting region.

name: Zwilag central interim storage facility, Würenlingen
status_note: Central interim store next to the Paul Scherrer Institute in Würenlingen (canton of Aargau) for all categories of Swiss radioactive waste: casks of spent fuel and vitrified high-level waste, plus intermediate- and low-level waste; it also runs a plasma plant and conditioning facilities. First spent fuel arrived in July 2001. Nagra plans the encapsulation plant for the future repository at this site.

name: Beishan Underground Research Laboratory
status_note: Granite underground research laboratory at the Xinchang site in the Beishan area of Gansu, the reference area for China's future HLW repository. Construction began in June 2021; the 7 km spiral ramp to 560 m was completed by January 2026 and research is to run for decades, with a repository possibly nearby by about 2050.
operator: China National Nuclear Corporation (Beijing Research Institute of Uranium Geology)

name: Daya Bay and Ling Ao Nuclear Power Plants
status_note: Daya Bay 1-2 (PWR, 1994) and the adjoining Ling Ao 1-4 (2002-2011) all operate. Daya Bay's pools reached capacity around 2003, since when part of its spent fuel has been shipped to the wet store at the pilot reprocessing plant in the Jiuquan complex; the rest stays in the site pools.
operator: Daya Bay Nuclear Power Operations and Management Co. (CGN)
notes: Covers both plants: Ling Ao lies about 1 km from Daya Bay and is run by the same operating company. The point marks Daya Bay.

name: Qinshan Nuclear Power Base (incl. Fangjiashan)
status_note: Multi-unit CNNC site at Qinshan, Haiyan County: Qinshan I (1994), Qinshan II-1 to II-4 (2002-2011), Qinshan III-1/2 (CANDU, 2002-2003) and Fangjiashan 1-2 (2014-2015), all operating. PWR fuel stays in the pools; CANDU fuel from Qinshan III has gone to on-site dry storage (MACSTOR-400 modules) since 2008.
notes: Includes Fangjiashan, about 1.5 km from Qinshan and part of the same CNNC base.

name: Beilong Disposal Facility (Guangdong)
status_note: Regional near-surface disposal facility in Guangdong with eight above-ground concrete disposal units, licensed in 2011. Listed as in operation in China's 2024 Joint Convention report, but a Korean study reports it has not received waste for over a decade and is planned to be closed.
notes: Position derived from descriptions (about 5-7 km north-east of the Daya Bay plant); it may be a few kilometres off.

name: Changjiang Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Units 1-2 (CNP-600, 2015-2016) and unit 3 (Hualong One, commercial September 2026) operate on Hainan; unit 4 and the ACP100 small modular reactor are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.
operator: CNNC (owners CNNC and China Huaneng Group)

name: Fangchenggang Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Units 1-2 (CPR-1000, 2015-2016) and 3-4 (Hualong One, 2023-2024) operate. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Feifengshan Low Level Solid Waste Disposal Facility (Sichuan)
status_note: Regional near-surface disposal facility in Sichuan with mound-type concrete units, licensed in 2016; Phase I Stage II (70,000 m3) entered operation after an October 2022 licence change.
operator: CNNC Sichuan Environmental Protection Engineering Co., Ltd.

name: Fuqing Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Six units operate: four CPR-1000 (2014-2017) and the first two Hualong One reactors (2021, 2022). Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Haiyang Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Two AP1000 units (2018, 2019) operate and units 3-5 (CAP1000) are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Hongyanhe Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Six units (CPR-1000/ACPR-1000, 2013-2022) operate in Liaoning. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Longhe Near Surface Disposal Facility (Gansu)
status_note: China's first centralised disposal facility for low-level waste from nuclear power plants, a semi-underground concrete structure with a planned capacity of 1 million m3 (40,000 m3 in Phase I Stage I). Licensed in July 2022 and receiving waste since November 2022.
operator: Gansu Longhe Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd.

name: Lop Nur nuclear test base
status_note: China's only nuclear test site: 45 tests from 16 October 1964 to 29 July 1996 (atmospheric, tower, air-drop and underground). China has observed a moratorium since 1996; satellite imagery since 2017 shows new shafts and infrastructure.
notes: Position of the first test (Project 596) ground zero; the underground test areas lie elsewhere in the base.

name: Ningde Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Units 1-4 (CPR-1000, 2013-2016) operate and units 5-6 (Hualong One) are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Northwest Low Level Solid Waste Disposal Facility (Gansu)
status_note: Near-surface disposal facility in Gansu with concrete disposal units, licensed in 2011; Phase I Stage II (90,000 m3) entered operation in April 2023. It has also received tens of thousands of disused sealed sources since 2019.

name: San'ao Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Unit 1 (Hualong One) entered commercial operation on 14 March 2026; units 2-4 are under construction. Discharged fuel will be held in the unit pool.
notes: With only one unit operating since early 2026, little or no spent fuel may have been discharged yet.

name: Sanmen Nuclear Power Station
status_note: Two AP1000 units (2018; unit 1 was the world's first AP1000 to reach criticality) operate; units 3-4 (CAP1000) are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Shidaowan (Shidao Bay) Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Site of the HTR-PM pebble-bed high-temperature gas-cooled demonstration plant (commercial December 2023) and two CAP1400/Guohe One PWRs (2024, 2025); two Hualong One units are under construction. Irradiated fuel from these reactors is held on site.
operator: Huaneng Shandong Shidao Bay Nuclear Power Co. and partners
notes: The PWR units may have a different owner (SPIC) from the HTR-PM (Huaneng); not confirmed. On-site storage of HTR-PM spent fuel pebbles is not described in the sources.

name: Taipingling Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Units 1 and 2 (Hualong One) entered commercial operation on 19 April and 3 August 2026; units 3-4 are under construction. Discharged fuel will be held in the unit pools.
notes: Both units started in 2026; little or no spent fuel may have been discharged yet.

name: Taishan Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Two EPR units (commercial 2018 and 2019); Taishan 1 was the first EPR anywhere to enter commercial operation. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.
operator: Taishan Nuclear Power Joint Venture Co. (CGN 70 %, EDF 30 %)

name: Tianwan Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Six units operate: four VVER-1000 (2007-2018) and two ACPR-1000 (2020-2021); units 7-8 (VVER-1200) are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Yangjiang Nuclear Power Station
status_note: Six CPR-1000/ACPR-1000 units (commercial 2014-2019) operate. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Zhangzhou Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: Units 1 and 2 (Hualong One) entered commercial operation on 1 January 2025 and 22 November 2025; units 3-4 are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the unit pools.

name: Richard Repository (Úložiště Richard), Litoměřice
status_note: Repository for institutional low- and intermediate-level waste in part of the former Richard II limestone mine beneath Bídnice hill near Litoměřice, in use since 1964. Disposal chambers hold about 10,250 m3 and are around 70% full.
notes: No published point for the portal; position of Radobýl hill, under which the complex was dug. SÚRAO places the mine beneath the adjoining Bídnice hill.

name: Dukovany nuclear power station
status_note: Four VVER-440 units (from 1985). Spent fuel is kept in the reactor pools and in on-site dry cask stores: the first (600 t) has operated since 1995 and a second store has been built since. Earlier, Dukovany fuel went to the Bohunice store in Slovakia and on to Russia.

name: Bratrství Repository (Úložiště Bratrství), Jáchymov
status_note: Repository in part of the former Bratrství uranium mine near Jáchymov, used since 1974 for institutional waste containing only natural radionuclides (capacity about 1,200 m3). SÚRAO reported in 2025 that the capacity is exhausted and new space in the access gallery needs regulatory approval.
notes: Holds radium and thorium sources, not uranium mining residue; 'NORM' is listed because only natural radionuclides are accepted.

name: Dukovany Repository (Úložiště Dukovany)
status_note: Near-surface repository of 112 reinforced concrete chambers (55,000 m3) inside the Dukovany NPP complex, in operation since 1995 for low-level operational waste from Dukovany and Temelín. About 20% full; it will never accept spent fuel.
notes: Position of the Dukovany power plant; the repository lies within the plant complex. It is a disposal facility, separate from the plant's spent fuel storage.

name: Hostim Repository (closed), Beroun
status_note: The country's first repository, in the abandoned Hostim I (Alkazar) limestone mine about 3 km east of Beroun. It received institutional waste from 1959 to 1964; higher-activity items were moved to Richard in 1964, and the remaining about 1,690 m3 of galleries were backfilled with concrete and finally closed in 1997. SÚRAO monitors the site.
notes: Position of a building in Beroun-Hostim, not the mine portal. Waste classes are inferred from the description as institutional waste.

name: Stráž pod Ralskem in-situ leaching remediation area
status_note: Decades of in-situ acid leaching of uranium contaminated a large aquifer; remediation by pumping and treating groundwater has been under way since 1996 and is expected to last until about 2037 at a total cost of about CZK 50 billion.

name: Temelín nuclear power station
status_note: Two VVER-1000 units (from 2002). Spent fuel is stored in the reracked reactor pools and in an on-site interim dry storage facility.

name: Konrad repository (Endlager Konrad)
status_note: Former iron ore mine in Salzgitter being converted into a repository for low- and intermediate-level waste with negligible heat generation, licensed in 2002 and confirmed by the courts in 2007. Capacity up to 303,000 m3; BGE plans to start disposal in the early 2030s.
notes: Position of the Konrad 1 shaft site in Salzgitter-Bleckenstedt; Konrad 2 lies about 1.5 km to the south-east.

name: Asse II mine (Schachtanlage Asse II)
status_note: Former potash and rock salt mine near Remlingen where about 126,000 drums (about 47,000 m3) of low- and intermediate-level waste were emplaced between 1967 and 1978. The mine is unstable and affected by brine inflow; BGE is legally required to retrieve the waste and then close the mine, with retrieval planned to start in 2033.
notes: 'Chemical' is listed because about 497 kg of arsenic, mercury and lead were emplaced. 'Decommissioning' reflects the legal mandate for retrieval and closure; retrieval has not begun.

name: Gorleben exploration mine (Erkundungsbergwerk Gorleben)
status_note: Salt dome explored underground from 1986 as a candidate high-level waste repository; no waste was ever emplaced. Exploration stopped in 2012 and the site was excluded from the national site selection in September 2020; closure was ordered and backfilling with salt began in late 2024.
notes: No radioactive waste was ever stored in the mine. Sources differ on the year of the closure order (2021 or 2022).

name: Morsleben repository (ERAM)
status_note: Former Bartensleben salt mine in Saxony-Anhalt used for about 37,000 m3 of low- and intermediate-level waste, emplaced from the early 1970s (GDR) and from 1994 to 1998, when emplacement stopped. BGE keeps the mine open while the licensing procedure for closure with the waste left in place is pending; the closure licence has not yet been granted.

name: AVR experimental reactor, Jülich (cask store)
status_note: Pebble-bed prototype reactor grid-connected 1967 to 1988. About 300,000 spent fuel pebbles in 152 CASTOR THTR/AVR casks are stored at the JEN site without a valid storage licence (expired 2013); transfer of the casks to Ahaus began on 25 March 2026.
notes: Position of the reactor; the cask store is on the neighbouring JEN site. The status will change to closed once all 152 casks are in Ahaus.

name: Ahaus interim storage facility (Zwischenlager Ahaus)
status_note: Central dry cask store in Ahaus-Ammeln holding six CASTOR V casks of power reactor spent fuel, 305 casks of spent fuel from the THTR-300 reactor, 18 casks from the Rossendorf research reactor and, since March 2026, casks from the AVR Jülich reactor. A separate hall holds about 360 containers of low- and intermediate-level waste destined for Konrad.
notes: The licence expiry for the spent fuel store is not stated; the waste store licence runs to 2057.

name: Biblis nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units, both shut down in 2011; the plant has been in decommissioning since 2017. The on-site interim store (in operation since May 2006) holds CASTOR casks with spent uranium and MOX fuel, plus six casks of vitrified waste returned from reprocessing abroad since November 2020.

name: Brokdorf nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, shut down on 31 December 2021; dismantling began in December 2024. Spent fuel is held in CASTOR casks in the on-site interim store (in operation since March 2007, licensed to 2047); the fuel pools were emptied into casks between 2023 and 2026.

name: Brunsbüttel nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, last operated in 2007 and in decommissioning since 2018. Twenty CASTOR V/52 casks with spent fuel are stored in the on-site interim store (in operation since 2006), which has had no valid storage licence since 2015 and operates under a regulatory order while a new licence is pending.

name: Gorleben cask storage facility (Transportbehälterlager Gorleben)
status_note: Central dry cask store next to the Gorleben salt dome holding 113 casks: 108 with vitrified high-level waste returned from reprocessing in France (last transport 2011) and 5 with spent fuel. The licence runs until 31 December 2034; BGZ applied in June 2026 for a 20-year extension.
notes: Operated by BGZ through its subsidiary Brennelementlager Gorleben GmbH.

name: Grafenrheinfeld nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, shut down in 2015 and being dismantled since 2018. Spent fuel is stored in CASTOR V/19 casks in the on-site interim store, in operation since February 2006.

name: Grohnde nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, shut down on 31 December 2021 and in decommissioning since 2023. Spent fuel is stored in CASTOR V/19 casks in the on-site interim store, in operation since April 2006.

name: Gundremmingen nuclear power plant
status_note: Three BWR units: A shut down in 1977, B in 2017 and C on 31 December 2021. Spent fuel is stored in CASTOR V/52 casks in the on-site interim store (in operation since 2006, licensed to 2046, 192 cask positions).

name: Heilbronn underground waste disposal facility (Steinsalzbergwerk Heilbronn)
status_note: Underground landfill for hazardous industrial waste in the Heilbronn rock salt mine. In 2026 the plan-approval procedure for continuing underground disposal and building a new disposal section was under way, with a public hearing on 29 July 2026.
notes: Position of the mine's surface site; the disposal areas are underground. The start of disposal (reported as 1987) is not confirmed.

name: Herfa-Neurode underground waste disposal facility
status_note: Underground landfill for hazardous industrial waste in a potash mine near Heringen (Werra), operating since 4 September 1972; more than 3.5 million tonnes of hazardous waste had been emplaced by 2023. Radioactive waste is excluded by the acceptance conditions.
notes: Position of the shaft site; the disposal fields extend underground beneath the surrounding area.

name: Isar nuclear power plant
status_note: Two units: Isar 1 (BWR) shut down in 2011 and Isar 2 (PWR) on 15 April 2023; the former Niederaichbach prototype (1973-1974, fuel sent to CEA in France, site returned to greenfield) stood at the same location. Spent fuel is stored in the on-site interim store (in operation since March 2007, licensed to 2047), which since April 2025 also holds seven casks of vitrified reprocessing waste.

name: KNK II fast reactor, Karlsruhe
status_note: Sodium-cooled prototype fast reactor on the Karlsruhe research site, shut down in 1991 and dismantled since 1993. Its spent fuel was transported to Cadarache (France) between 1989 and 1994 for reprocessing.
notes: The neighbouring MZFR heavy-water reactor on the same site is not listed separately.

name: Kahl and Großwelzheim nuclear power plants (Karlstein am Main)
status_note: Site of the Kahl experimental BWR (1961-1985) and the Großwelzheim superheated-steam BWR (1969-1971). Both plants have been fully dismantled (Großwelzheim by 1998, Kahl by 2008) and the site released.
notes: The destination of the spent fuel is not documented; its removal is inferred from the dismantling of both plants and the unrestricted release of the Kahl site.

name: Krümmel nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, out of power operation since 2011. Spent uranium and MOX fuel is stored in CASTOR V/52 casks in the on-site interim store, in operation since November 2006.

name: Lingen and Emsland nuclear power plants
status_note: Two neighbouring plants: the Lingen prototype BWR (shut down 1977, in safe enclosure/dismantling) and the Emsland PWR (shut down on 15 April 2023). The Lingen interim store on the site has held CASTOR V/19 casks with spent fuel since December 2002.
notes: Position of the old Lingen plant, where the store is located; the Emsland plant lies about 1.3 km away. Where the Lingen prototype fuel went is not confirmed.

name: Mülheim-Kärlich nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, operated briefly in 1987-1988 and being dismantled. The fuel was removed in 2002 and shipped to La Hague for reprocessing.
notes: The operator name has not been confirmed in a primary source.

name: Neckarwestheim nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units: Neckarwestheim I shut down in 2011, Neckarwestheim II on 15 April 2023. The on-site interim store (in operation since December 2006) holds CASTOR casks with spent fuel from Neckarwestheim and, since 2017, the 342 spent fuel assemblies from Obrigheim.

name: Obrigheim nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, shut down in 2005 and being dismantled. Its 342 spent fuel assemblies were kept in an external wet store on site until they were shipped to the Neckarwestheim interim store in 2017; no high-level waste store remains.

name: Philippsburg nuclear power plant
status_note: Two units: Philippsburg 1 (BWR) shut down in 2011 and Philippsburg 2 (PWR) in 2019; the site has been in decommissioning since 2020. Spent fuel is stored in CASTOR V/19 and V/52 casks in the on-site interim store, in operation since March 2007.

name: Rheinsberg nuclear power plant
status_note: One VVER-70 unit, operated 1966 to 1990 and being dismantled by EWN. All high-level material, including spent fuel, has been moved to the Zwischenlager Nord at Lubmin (confirmed by EWN in November 2025).

name: Stade nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, operated from 1972 to 2003 and being dismantled. The last fuel left the site in April 2005; a store for low- and intermediate-level waste is licensed on site until 2046.
notes: The operator and the destination of the last fuel are not confirmed.

name: THTR-300 Hamm-Uentrop
status_note: Thorium high-temperature pebble-bed reactor, operated 1987 to 1989. The fuel was unloaded between 1993 and 1995 and taken to the Ahaus interim store; the reactor is in safe enclosure.

name: Unterweser nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit, shut down in 2011 and in decommissioning since 2018. Spent fuel is stored in CASTOR V/19 casks in the on-site interim store, in operation since June 2007.

name: Wismut Crossen mill and Helmsdorf tailings pond
status_note: The Crossen mill near Zwickau (1950 to 1989, 74.7 million t of ore) processed ore from all major Wismut deposits; its tailings went to the Helmsdorf pond. Helmsdorf is one of Wismut's four industrial tailings ponds being dewatered, stabilised and covered in place, with work scheduled until 2028.
notes: The link between the Helmsdorf pond and the Crossen mill is not stated explicitly in the sources.

name: Wismut Königstein uranium mine (former underground leaching)
status_note: Sandstone uranium deposit in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains about 40 km south-east of Dresden, discovered in 1963 and mined from 1967 to 1990, partly by leaching of blasted ore underground. Large volumes of uranium-bearing solution had to be treated before and during the controlled flooding; in 2025 about 213 m3/h of flooding water (about 4.5 mg/l uranium in the inflow) was treated before discharge to the Elbe.
notes: Position of Leupoldishain village; the deposit lies beneath the area between Königstein and Pirna.

name: Wismut Ronneburg uranium mining site (incl. backfilled Lichtenberg open pit)
status_note: Largest Wismut mining area in eastern Thuringia (black-shale uranium ore, mined from 1950 to 1990). Most waste rock dumps were relocated into the Lichtenberg open pit; the flooded mine is kept at about 247 m above sea level and about 470 m3/h of mine and ground water were treated in 2025 before discharge to the Wipse.
notes: Position of the reclaimed 'Neue Landschaft Ronneburg' area; the former mining field is larger.

name: Wismut Schlema-Alberoda uranium mine (Aue)
status_note: Largest vein-type uranium deposit of the Ore Mountains, mined by Wismut from 1946 until 31 December 1990 to depths of over 700 m at Oberschlema and deeper at Niederschlema-Alberoda. The mine has been flooded since 1991; in 2025 about 543 m3/h of flooding water, loaded with uranium and arsenic, was treated before discharge to the Zwickauer Mulde.
notes: Position of Schacht 371 (Hartenstein), seat of the Wismut Aue division.

name: Wismut Seelingstädt mill and Culmitzsch tailings ponds
status_note: The Seelingstädt mill (from 1961) processed most Wismut ore and used the former Culmitzsch open pits as tailings ponds. Wismut's four industrial tailings ponds hold about 160 million m3 of tailings on about 700 ha; their in-situ stabilisation and covering is scheduled to run until 2028. About 143 m3/h of seepage and pore water was treated at Seelingstädt in 2025.
notes: Position of Culmitzsch village. The 160 million m3 and 700 ha figures cover all four Wismut tailings ponds, not Culmitzsch alone.

name: Würgassen nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, operated 1971 to 1994 and dismantled by 2014. Spent fuel was delivered to Cogema (France) for reprocessing; two interim stores for low- and intermediate-level waste remain on site.
operator: BGZ Gesellschaft für Zwischenlagerung (one of the waste stores)

name: Zielitz underground waste disposal facility
status_note: Underground landfill for hazardous waste in the Zielitz potash mine north of Magdeburg, one of two underground disposal sites run by K+S.
notes: Start date and waste quantities are not documented in the sources.

name: Zwischenlager Nord (ZLN), Lubmin
status_note: Interim store on the site of the former Greifswald nuclear power plant. Hall 8 holds 74 CASTOR casks, mostly spent fuel from the Greifswald and Rheinsberg reactors plus fuel from the KNK reactor and the ship Otto Hahn, and five casks of vitrified waste from the Karlsruhe reprocessing plant; the other halls store and treat low- and intermediate-level decommissioning waste. A replacement cask store (ESTRAL) is planned next to it.
notes: The remaining casks are assumed to hold Greifswald and Rheinsberg fuel; the source does not state this explicitly. The licence status of ESTRAL is not confirmed.

name: Risø waste storage (Danish Decommissioning)
status_note: Interim storage of all Danish radioactive waste from medicine, industry and research and from decommissioning of the former Risø nuclear research reactors, near Roskilde. A flood-resistant new storage facility is planned; under Parliament resolution B 90 (2018) a deep repository is to operate by 2073, and Danish Decommissioning submitted a site-neutral repository proposal on 2 October 2026.
notes: No inventory is published; 'intermediate-level' is inferred from plans for 'the most radioactive waste'. The waste is to stay at Risø until 2073 at the latest.

name: In Ekker underground test site (Taourirt Tan Afella), CEMO
status_note: French underground tests in galleries in the Taourirt Tan Afella granite massif near In Ekker, about 150 km north of Tamanrasset: 13 underground tests up to 1966. In the Béryl test on 1 May 1962 the gallery seal failed and radioactive lava and gas escaped.
notes: Position of the Béryl incident. No source on the current state of the site was found.

name: Reggane (Hamoudia) atmospheric test site, CSEM
status_note: French Centre Saharien d'Expérimentations Militaires at Hamoudia, about 50 km south of Reggane: four atmospheric tests (Gerboise Bleue, Blanche, Rouge and Verte) from 13 February 1960 to 25 April 1961.
notes: Position of the Gerboise Bleue ground zero; Gerboise Verte was at 26°19'18"N 0°04'24"W. No source on current management was found.

name: Paldiski former naval reactor site and interim radioactive waste storage
status_note: Former Soviet submarine training centre with two land-based training reactors (shut down 1989, defuelled and sealed in concrete sarcophagi by 1995). An interim store for Estonian radioactive waste was set up in the main reactor building in 1997. Final dismantling of the reactor compartments is planned from around 2040 and needs a national repository, for which land next to the site has been considered.
notes: Position estimated from the site address, about 4 km north-east of Paldiski. The reactor vessels hold activated components (Co-60) but no fuel.

name: Sillamäe radioactive tailings pond
status_note: The Sillamäe plant extracted uranium from local and imported ores from about 1950 to 1989 and dumped the processing waste into a tailings pond on the Baltic shore north-west of the town. Measures to secure the containment and stop leaching into the Baltic Sea were carried out in the 2000s.
notes: Position of Sillamäe town; the pond lies on its north-western edge.

name: El Cabril disposal centre (Sierra Albarrana)
status_note: Spain's national near-surface disposal facility for low-, intermediate- and very-low-level solid waste in the Sierra Albarrana (Hornachuelos, Córdoba), with final operating authorisation since October 2001 and an authorised volume of 165,000 m3. At the end of 2025 the 28 LILW vaults were 84.87% full; the new South-East platform for LILW is to be built from 2027 and operate from 2031.

name: Almaraz nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units (commercial operation 1981 and 1983), licensed in August 2026 to operate until 8 June 2030. Spent fuel is stored in the pools and in an on-site dry storage facility (ATI).

name: Ascó nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units in operation since the mid-1980s. Spent fuel is stored in the pools and in an on-site dry storage facility (ATI).

name: Cofrentes nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, licensed until November 2030. Spent fuel is stored in the pool and in an on-site dry storage facility (ATI).

name: José Cabrera (Zorita) nuclear power plant
status_note: One small PWR unit, operated 1968-2006 and dismantled by Enresa since 2010. Its spent fuel is kept on site in a dry storage facility (ATI).

name: Palomares plutonium contamination site (1966 B-52 accident)
status_note: On 17 January 1966 two hydrogen bombs from a crashed USAF B-52 broke open on land near Palomares (Almería), spreading plutonium over about 2 km2. About 1,750 t of soil were shipped to the USA, but residual contamination remained; plots were expropriated after 2004 and Spain and the USA agreed in 2015 to negotiate further clean-up.
notes: Some contamination remained as of 2025; whether the 2015 statement of intent led to soil removal is not confirmed.

name: Santa María de Garoña nuclear power plant
status_note: One BWR unit, operated 1971-2012; dismantling began in July 2023. Spent fuel is being moved from the pool into an on-site dry storage facility (first cask placed July 2022, expansion approved May 2025).

name: Trillo nuclear power plant
status_note: One PWR unit (Trillo 1), in operation since 1988. Spent fuel is stored in the pool and in an on-site dry cask store, the first in Spain.

name: Vandellòs nuclear power plant
status_note: Vandellòs 1 (UNGG gas-graphite, 1972-1990) is in safe storage after partial dismantling; its fuel was reprocessed. Vandellòs 2 (PWR) operates and keeps all its spent fuel in the pool; an on-site ATI dry store for up to 73 casks was authorised in November 2024 and is due in service before April 2027.
notes: Reprocessing of the Vandellòs 1 fuel is inferred from references to high-level waste from that fuel.

name: Onkalo spent fuel repository (Olkiluoto)
status_note: Deep geological repository for spent fuel from the Olkiluoto and Loviisa reactors, with an encapsulation plant, on Olkiluoto island in Eurajoki. The Finnish government granted Posiva the operating licence on 22 October 2026 (up to 6,500 tU) after a positive STUK safety assessment in August 2026; disposal may only start after commissioning tests and a STUK pre-commissioning inspection, and no start date has been set.
notes: The licence also covers limited low- and intermediate-level waste from the encapsulation plant and repository; only spent fuel is listed as the main waste type.

name: Olkiluoto nuclear power plant (incl. KPA spent fuel store)
status_note: Three units: Olkiluoto 1 and 2 (BWR, 1978-1980) and Olkiluoto 3 (EPR, regular operation since 2023). Spent fuel is kept in the on-site KPA interim pool store, in operation since 1987 and doubled with three new pools ordered in 2010; the Onkalo repository on the same island received its operating licence in October 2026.
notes: The KPA store has operated since 1987. Onkalo is a separate entry.

name: Loviisa nuclear power plant
status_note: Two VVER-440 units (1977 and 1980), licensed to 2050. Spent fuel was returned to Mayak in Russia until 1996; since then it has been kept on site in interim storage pools, expanded in 2000.

name: Loviisa VLJ repository for low- and intermediate-level waste (Hästholmen)
status_note: Rock-cavern repository at 110 m depth on Hästholmen island at the Loviisa nuclear power plant, in operation since 1998 for operational low- and intermediate-level waste. A new licence of March 2023 allows operation until 2090 and adds disposal of up to 50,000 m3 of decommissioning waste.
notes: Position of Hästholmen island, which hosts both the power plant and the repository.

name: Olkiluoto VLJ repository for low- and intermediate-level waste
status_note: Rock-cavern repository with two silos at 60-100 m depth on Olkiluoto island for operational low- and intermediate-level waste from the Olkiluoto plant and small amounts from healthcare, industry and research, in operation since 1992. It was about half full (about 5,500 m3) in 2012.
notes: Position of the Olkiluoto power plant, not the repository caverns, which lie at 60-100 m, shallower than typical deep repositories.

name: Centre de stockage de la Manche (CSM)
status_note: France's first near-surface disposal facility, next to the La Hague reprocessing plant, received about 527,000 m3 of low- and intermediate-level waste from 1969 to 1994. It has been covered and in a monitoring phase since a 2003 decree, planned to last about 300 years.

name: Centre de stockage de l'Aube (CSA)
status_note: Near-surface disposal facility at Soulaines-Dhuys for short-lived low- and intermediate-level waste, operating since January 1992. Capacity is about 1 million m3; it was 36.3% full at the end of 2021 and is expected to operate for about 50 more years, followed by about 300 years of monitoring.

name: Belleville nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P'4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Blayais nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (CP1) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Brennilis (Monts d'Arrée, EL-4) nuclear power plant
status_note: Experimental 70 MWe heavy-water gas-cooled reactor, shut down in 1985; a dismantling licence was issued in 2006 and dismantling is in progress.
notes: Removal of the spent fuel is assumed from the decommissioning status but is not confirmed.

name: Bugey nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (Bugey 2-5) in operation; the UNGG gas-graphite unit Bugey 1 (shut down 1994) is being dismantled. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Cattenom nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P'4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Chinon nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (Chinon B) in operation; the three UNGG gas-graphite units of Chinon A (shut down 1973-1990) are being dismantled. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Chooz nuclear power plant
status_note: Two N4 PWR units (Chooz B) in operation; the prototype PWR Chooz A (305 MWe) has been under dismantling since its 2007 licence. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Cigéo deep geological repository (planned), Bure
status_note: Planned repository at about 500 m depth in Callovo-Oxfordian clay on the border of the Meuse and Haute-Marne départements for high-level and long-lived intermediate-level waste (about 83,000 m3). Andra applied for the creation licence in January 2023; the ASNR issued its technical opinion in December 2025 and the public inquiry commission gave a favourable opinion in August 2026, but the authorisation decree has not been signed.
notes: Position of Bure village; the facility is planned a few kilometres north of the Bure laboratory. Sources differ on first waste: about 2045 (Andra schedule) or 2050.

name: Cires very-low-level waste disposal facility (Morvilliers)
status_note: Andra's industrial centre for grouping, storage and disposal at Morvilliers and La Chaise (Aube), disposing of very-low-level waste since 2003. It was 69.4% full at the end of 2022; in July 2024 the authorised capacity was raised from 650,000 to 950,000 m3 without enlarging the disposal area.
notes: Position of the 'Centre de stockage de Morvilliers', assumed to be Cires (Andra's only facility in Morvilliers).

name: Civaux nuclear power plant
status_note: Two N4 PWR units in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Cruas-Meysse nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (CP2) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Dampierre nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (CP1) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Fessenheim nuclear power plant
status_note: Two PWR units, permanently shut down in 2020. All spent fuel was shipped from the pools to Orano La Hague by August 2022; the plant is being prepared for dismantling.

name: Flamanville nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units and the EPR Flamanville 3, the most recently grid-connected French reactor, in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Golfech nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P'4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Gravelines nuclear power plant
status_note: Six 900 MWe-class PWR units (CP1) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: La Hague reprocessing plant (Orano)
status_note: Spent fuel reprocessing complex on the Cotentin peninsula, operating since 1976. Spent fuel awaiting reprocessing is held in large pools whose margins are reduced, with the regulator seeing a risk of saturation from the early 2030s; vitrified high-level waste (CSD-V) and compacted waste (CSD-C) are stored on site pending disposal in Cigéo. The older UP2-400 plant is being dismantled.
notes: The Centre de stockage de la Manche lies directly to the east.

name: Marcoule nuclear site (UP1 reprocessing plant and legacy waste)
status_note: Nuclear site in the Gard where France's first reprocessing plant, UP1, operated; it is being decommissioned. Most of UP1's waste was stored without treatment, partly in bulk, and is being retrieved and repackaged, which may take several decades. The site also hosts the Melox MOX plant and research facilities.
notes: Also a former plutonium production site (G1-G3 reactors). The CEA as operator of the legacy waste programme is assumed, not confirmed.

name: Meuse/Haute-Marne Underground Research Laboratory (Bure)
status_note: Andra's underground laboratory with galleries at about 490 m depth in Callovo-Oxfordian claystone, built from 2000 and in service since 2007, used to study the host rock for the planned Cigéo repository. No radioactive waste is stored there.

name: Nogent nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P'4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Paluel nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Penly nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P'4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Saint-Alban nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 1300 MWe-class PWR units (P4) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Saint-Laurent nuclear power plant
status_note: Two 900 MWe-class PWR units (St-Laurent B, CP2) in operation; the two UNGG gas-graphite units of St-Laurent A (shut down 1990 and 1992) are being dismantled. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Superphénix and APEC fuel store (Creys-Malville)
status_note: Superphénix, a 1200 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder, operated from 1986 and was shut down in 1997-1998; it is being dismantled. Its fuel is stored on site in the APEC facility (INB 141), which has a pool storage building and a dry storage building.
notes: The APEC also stores sodium-concrete blocks from sodium neutralisation, listed as intermediate-level; that classification is not confirmed.

name: Tricastin nuclear power plant
status_note: Four 900 MWe-class PWR units (CP1) in operation. Spent fuel is kept in the fuel building pools until it is shipped to Orano La Hague for reprocessing; there is no on-site dry storage.
notes: Storage practice reflects general EDF practice (cooling in on-site pools, then transport to La Hague), not a site-specific source.

name: Mounana former uranium mine and mill (COMUF)
status_note: COMUF mined and milled uranium around Mounana from 1961 to 1999 (nearly 28,000 t U). Over 2 million t of tailings were released into a creek before 1975 and about 4 million t dumped in the former open pit; covers of laterite and rock were placed and reclamation was declared complete in July 2004, though NGOs doubt its long-term effectiveness.
notes: The main source is an NGO page last updated in 2004.

name: Low Level Waste Repository (LLWR), near Drigg
status_note: The UK's national near-surface disposal facility for low-level waste near Drigg in Cumbria, receiving waste since 1959, with Sellafield as its largest source. Full historic trenches and vaults are being permanently capped; work began in 2023 and is planned to take about five years.

name: Sellafield
status_note: Former reprocessing complex in Cumbria: THORP stopped reprocessing in 2018 and the Magnox reprocessing plant was due to close in July 2022, ending reprocessing in the UK. The site continues to store spent fuel from the UK AGR fleet and manages high-, intermediate- and low-level waste, while retrieving waste and sludge from its legacy ponds and silos.
notes: 'Decommissioning' reflects the end of reprocessing and the clean-up mission, although large stores remain in operation.

name: Dounreay (incl. low-level waste vaults)
status_note: Former fast reactor research and fuel cycle site in Caithness under decommissioning. Conditioned higher-activity waste is stored above ground on site, low-level waste goes to adjacent shallow engineered vaults, and legacy waste in a 65 m shaft, a silo and shallow pits is to be retrieved; the timing of the interim end state is under review.
notes: Since April 2023 part of Magnox Ltd, now Nuclear Restoration Services. Waste types are mapped from the site's own terms ('high-active', 'low-active').

name: Harwell nuclear site (former UKAEA research establishment)
status_note: Former Atomic Energy Research Establishment, founded in 1946, with early research reactors and laboratories. Nuclear Restoration Services is dismantling the legacy facilities and has delicensed 23 hectares for the Harwell Science and Innovation Campus; radioactive waste accumulation and decommissioning remain regulated by ONR.
notes: Position of the Harwell Campus, which contains the remaining licensed nuclear area. The remaining ILW and LLW stores are assumed, not confirmed.

name: Trawsfynydd nuclear power station
status_note: Two Magnox reactors, shut down in 1991. Spent fuel was removed to Sellafield by rail between 1993 and 1997. Intermediate-level waste is retrieved, packaged and kept in an on-site interim store.
notes: No longer holds spent fuel; included because of the intermediate-level waste store.

name: Berkeley nuclear power station
status_note: Two Magnox reactors, shut down in 1988 and 1989; the first UK commercial station to be decommissioned. All Magnox spent fuel was shipped to Sellafield; the defuelling programme for the whole Magnox fleet ended at Wylfa in 2019. Intermediate-level waste is stored on site, and in 2013 the NDA chose Berkeley as the interim store for Oldbury ILW.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Bradwell nuclear power station
status_note: Two Magnox reactors, shut down in 2002. All Magnox spent fuel was shipped to Sellafield; the defuelling programme for the whole Magnox fleet ended at Wylfa in 2019. The site is in decommissioning with the reactor buildings and intermediate-level waste remaining on site.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Chapelcross nuclear power station
status_note: Four Magnox reactors; generation ceased in June 2004 and defuelling was completed in February 2013. The reactors are free of spent fuel; care and maintenance is planned until the 2080s, with final site clearance about 2089-2095.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Dungeness nuclear power stations (A and B)
status_note: Dungeness A (two Magnox reactors) ceased generation in 2006 and was defuelled by June 2012, with all fuel sent to Sellafield. Dungeness B (two AGRs, 1983/1985) entered defuelling in June 2021; its spent fuel is being shipped to Sellafield in flasks, a process EDF expects to take three to five years.
operator: EDF Energy (Dungeness B); Nuclear Restoration Services (Dungeness A)
notes: Completion of Dungeness B defuelling is not confirmed.

name: Hartlepool nuclear power station
status_note: Two AGR units in operation since 1983, with life extensions announced to about 2030. Spent fuel is cooled in the station pond and shipped by rail to Sellafield.
notes: Sources give the closure date as March 2028 or March 2030.

name: Heysham 1 and 2 nuclear power stations
status_note: Four AGR units in two stations (Heysham 1 from 1983, Heysham 2 from 1988), with life extensions to about 2028-2030. Spent fuel is cooled in the station ponds and shipped by rail to Sellafield.

name: Hinkley Point A and B nuclear power stations
status_note: Hinkley Point A (two Magnox reactors) shut down in 2000 and has been defuelled. Hinkley Point B (two AGRs, from 1976) ended generation in August 2022 and defuelling was complete by December 2025, with the fuel shipped to Sellafield. Intermediate-level waste and the reactor cores remain on site; Hinkley Point C is under construction next door.
operator: EDF Energy (Hinkley Point B); Nuclear Restoration Services (Hinkley Point A)

name: Hunterston A and B nuclear power stations
status_note: Hunterston A (two Magnox reactors) closed in 1989-1990 and has been defuelled. Hunterston B (two AGRs, from 1976) was defuelled between 2022 and April 2025, when the site was declared fuel-free, and transferred to Nuclear Restoration Services on 1 April 2026. Intermediate-level waste remains on site.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Oldbury nuclear power station
status_note: Two Magnox reactors, shut down in 2011 and 2012 and since defuelled. All Magnox spent fuel was shipped to Sellafield; the defuelling programme for the whole Magnox fleet ended at Wylfa in 2019. Oldbury intermediate-level waste is planned to be stored at nearby Berkeley.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Sizewell A and B nuclear power stations
status_note: Sizewell A (two Magnox reactors) shut down in 2006 and has been defuelled. Sizewell B (PWR, operating since 1995) stores spent fuel in its pool and, since the mid-2010s, in an on-site dry fuel store built from 2014 because the pool was nearly full.
operator: EDF Energy (Sizewell B); Nuclear Restoration Services (Sizewell A)

name: Torness nuclear power station
status_note: Two AGR units, commissioned 1988-1989 and expected to operate until March 2030. Spent fuel is cooled in the station pond and shipped by rail to Sellafield.

name: Wylfa nuclear power station
status_note: Two Magnox reactors; unit 2 shut down in 2012 and unit 1 in December 2015, the last Magnox reactor to operate. Defuelling ran from 2016 to September 2019, with the fuel shipped to Sellafield.
notes: Included although defuelled, because the reactor cores and other intermediate-level waste remain on site during a long care-and-maintenance period.

name: Hurd Deep radioactive waste dumping site (English Channel)
status_note: Packaged radioactive waste from the United Kingdom was dumped in Hurd Deep, a trench north-west of the Channel Islands at 65-160 m depth; the IAEA inventory lists UK dumping at this position in most years from 1950 to 1963. The waste remains on the seabed without active management.
notes: Sources differ: IAEA gives 1950-1963 at 49°50'N 2°18'W, Wikipedia 1946-1973 with about 28,500 barrels. The IAEA position lies in Guernsey's territorial sea.

name: Thule (Pituffik) B-52 crash site, North Star Bay
status_note: On 21 January 1968 a USAF B-52 carrying four hydrogen bombs crashed onto sea ice in North Star Bay; the conventional explosives detonated and dispersed plutonium. Project Crested Ice removed contaminated ice and debris, but part of the material, including the secondary stage of one weapon, was never recovered and remains on the seabed.
notes: The impact area lies about 12 km west of the air base.

name: Radioactive Waste Management Centre Čerkezovac, Trgovska gora
status_note: Planned centre at the former Čerkezovac army barracks on Trgovska gora (Dvor municipality, on the border with Bosnia and Herzegovina) for long-term storage of Croatia's half of the low- and intermediate-level waste from the Krško NPP and of Croatian institutional waste. Parliament passed an enabling law in December 2025; site clearing was under way in April 2026 while the environmental impact assessment was still pending.
operator: Fund for Financing the Decommissioning of the Krško NPP and the Disposal of NEK Radioactive Waste and Spent Fuel (Fond NEK)
notes: No coordinates found; position of Dvor town (the site is on Trgovska gora in the same municipality). Bosnia and Herzegovina opposes the project.

name: National Radioactive Waste Repository (NRHT), Bátaapáti
status_note: Underground repository in the Mórágy granite at about 200-250 m depth for low- and intermediate-level waste from the Paks NPP. First waste was emplaced on 5 December 2012; further disposal chambers have been built since while operation continues.
operator: PURAM / RHK Kft. (Public Limited Company for Radioactive Waste Management)
notes: Position of Bátaapáti village; the licence gives the site only in national grid coordinates.

name: Paks nuclear power plant (incl. KKÁT dry store)
status_note: Four VVER-440 units (started 1982-1987), with lifetime extension planned to 70 years. Spent fuel is kept in the pools for about five years and then moved to the on-site interim dry storage facility (KKÁT, designed for 50 years); some fuel was earlier returned to Russia.
operator: MVM Paks Nuclear Power Plant Ltd

name: Radioactive Waste Treatment and Disposal Facility (RHFT), Püspökszilágy
status_note: Near-surface facility of concrete vaults and wells on a hill near Püspökszilágy, about 40-50 km north-east of Budapest, operating since the 1970s. Since 1996 it accepts only institutional low- and intermediate-level waste; a safety improvement programme including retrieval and repackaging of old waste has been running in stages since 2009.
operator: RHK Kft. (Public Limited Company for Radioactive Waste Management)
notes: Position of Püspökszilágy village; the facility is on a nearby hill. Tritium in groundwater within the controlled zone has been reported but not confirmed by the regulator.

name: Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (Rawatbhata)
status_note: Unit 1 (CANDU, 1973) has been shut down since 2004 pending decommissioning; units 2-7 (PHWR, 1981-2025) operate and unit 8 is under construction. An AFR spent fuel store has operated on site since 2005, and in 2026 the regulator gave construction consent for phase 1 of an additional AFR facility for units 2-6.
operator: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL)

name: Tarapur Atomic Power Station
status_note: Units 1-2 (BWR, 1969), India's oldest, and units 3-4 (PHWR, 2005-2006) operate; unit 1 returned to criticality on 30 December 2025 after a life-extension outage since 2020. Besides the reactor pools, two away-from-reactor (AFR) spent fuel stores operate on site, AFR-1 since 1990 and AFR-2 since 2012.
operator: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL)
notes: Spent fuel is stored pending reprocessing (India follows a closed fuel cycle).

name: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay (plutonium plant and Waste Immobilisation Plant)
status_note: India's oldest reprocessing plant (from 1964, about 60 t/year), handling research reactor fuel and historically supplying weapons plutonium. High-level liquid waste is vitrified at the Trombay Waste Immobilisation Plant (permanent facility since 2013) and vitrified waste is held in interim storage.
operator: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Department of Atomic Energy
notes: Position of the BARC headquarters.

name: Kaiga Generating Station
status_note: Four PHWR units (IPHWR-220, commercial 2000-2011; unit 1 currently in a maintenance outage); units 5-6 (IPHWR-700) are under construction. Spent fuel is held in the on-site storage bays.
operator: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL)

name: Kakrapar Atomic Power Station
status_note: Units 1-2 (IPHWR-220, 1993 and 1995) and units 3-4 (IPHWR-700, commercial 2023 and 2024), all operating. Spent fuel is held in the on-site storage bays.
operator: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL)

name: Kalpakkam Reprocessing Plant (KARP / KARP-II) and fast reactor fuel reprocessing
status_note: PHWR fuel reprocessing at Kalpakkam (KARP, 100 t/year, back in service after a 2003-2009 outage, capacity doubled with KARP-II) with an adjacent waste immobilisation plant. IGCAR on the same complex runs CORAL and the Demonstration Fast Reactor Fuel Reprocessing Plant for fast breeder test reactor fuel.
operator: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)
notes: Position of IGCAR. The Madras power station on the same campus is a separate entry.

name: Kalpakkam: Madras Atomic Power Station and Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor
status_note: MAPS-1 and MAPS-2 (PHWR, 1984 and 1986; unit 1 currently in a maintenance outage) and the sodium-cooled Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor, which was loaded with fuel from October 2025 and reached first criticality on 6 April 2026. MAPS spent fuel is sent for reprocessing; an interim storage facility also exists at Kalpakkam.
notes: Covers only the power reactors; the reprocessing facilities on the Kalpakkam campus are a separate entry.

name: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant
