operator: R.E. Ginna Nuclear Power Plant, LLC (Constellation)

name: Rancho Seco (ISFSI)
status_note: PWR shut down in 1989 and decommissioned; spent fuel is stored at the site-specifically licensed ISFSI (SNM-2510), whose licence renewal for a further 40 years was under NRC review in 2020.

name: River Bend Station
status_note: One BWR unit in operation (operating licence 1985). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Salem Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1976 and 1981); adjacent to Hope Creek. Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: Unit 1 (1968-1992) and Units 2 and 3 (shut down 2013) are being dismantled. All fuel from the three units has been in the on-site ISFSI (Holtec UMAX for Units 2 and 3) since August 2020.

name: Savannah River Site
status_note: Former plutonium and tritium production complex in South Carolina. About 32 million gallons of liquid high-level waste remain in 43 underground tanks; the Defense Waste Processing Facility has vitrified waste into about 4,500 canisters since 1996 (about 7,440 projected), stored on site.
operator: US Department of Energy (Savannah River Nuclear Solutions; Savannah River Mission Completion for liquid waste)
notes: The site spans parts of three counties. Spent fuel storage (L-Basin) is assumed but not confirmed by the sources.

name: Seabrook Station
status_note: One PWR unit in operation (operating licence 1990). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Sequoyah Nuclear Plant
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1980 and 1981). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Shearon Harris Nuclear Power Plant
status_note: One PWR unit in operation (operating licence 1986). Spent fuel is stored in the plant's pool(s); the site was not shown with a dry storage ISFSI on the NRC's June 2023 ISFSI map.
notes: In June 2023 Harris had not announced plans for dry storage; later plans are not confirmed.

name: Shoreham Nuclear Power Station
status_note: BWR licensed in 1986 but run only at low power before abandonment in 1989; its lightly irradiated fuel was shipped to Limerick and the plant was decommissioned (licence terminated).

name: South Texas Project
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1988 and 1989). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: St. Lucie Plant
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1976 and 1983). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Surry Power Station
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1972 and 1973); site of the first NRC-licensed dry storage installation (1986). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI (site-specific and general NRC licences).

name: Susquehanna Steam Electric Station
status_note: Two BWR units in operation (operating licences 1982 and 1984). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Three Mile Island / Christopher M. Crane Clean Energy Center
status_note: Unit 1 (renamed Crane Clean Energy Center in 2025) shut down on 26 September 2019 and Constellation is pursuing a restart; its spent fuel has been moved into dry storage at the on-site ISFSI. Unit 2 was damaged in the 1979 accident; its core debris is stored by DOE in Idaho and Unit 2 is being decommissioned.
operator: Constellation Energy Generation, LLC (Unit 1); TMI-2 Solutions (Unit 2)
notes: About 1 percent of the TMI-2 core remains as fuel debris in the Unit 2 plant (NRC).

name: Trojan (ISFSI)
status_note: PWR operated 1976-1992 and was decommissioned; since 2003 its 791 spent fuel assemblies have been held in 34 dry casks at the ISFSI near Rainier.

name: Turkey Point Nuclear Generating Station
status_note: Two nuclear PWR units (3 and 4) in operation (operating licences 1972 and 1973). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: US Ecology Richland commercial LLW disposal site (Hanford Site)
status_note: Commercial low-level waste site on about 100 acres leased to Washington State near the centre of the Hanford Site, about 23 miles north-west of Richland; open since 1965, waste is buried in unlined trenches. Serves the Northwest Compact and, since 1993, the Rocky Mountain Compact states.
notes: Position derived from a state monitoring report (just south-west of the Hanford 200 East Area).

name: Vermont Yankee Nuclear Power Station
status_note: Single BWR shut down on 29 December 2014 and being decommissioned. All 2,996 spent fuel assemblies have been in 58 dry casks at the on-site ISFSI since August 2018; transfer to DOE is assumed by 2052.

name: Virgil C. Summer Nuclear Station
status_note: One PWR unit in operation (operating licence 1982). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Vogtle Electric Generating Plant
status_note: Four PWR units in operation: Units 1 and 2 (operating licences 1987 and 1989) and AP1000 Units 3 and 4 (NRC 52.103(g) findings 2022 and 2023). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Waste Control Specialists, Andrews County (Texas Compact LLW disposal)
status_note: Commercial site east of Eunice (New Mexico) licensed since 2009 to dispose of Class A, B and C low-level waste and to store Greater-than-Class-C waste; host of the Texas Compact disposal facility and a federal waste facility.
operator: Waste Control Specialists LLC (J.F. Lehman & Company)
notes: US Class B/C waste is shown as intermediate-level; US classes do not map one-to-one. Operating status is not confirmed by a primary source.

name: Waterford Steam Electric Station
status_note: One PWR unit (Unit 3) in operation (operating licence 1985). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Watts Bar Nuclear Plant
status_note: Two PWR units in operation (operating licences 1996 and 2015). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: West Valley Demonstration Project (former NFS reprocessing plant)
status_note: Site of the only US commercial reprocessing plant (1966-1972), about 30 miles south of Buffalo. Liquid high-level waste was vitrified into 275 canisters by 2002, which stay on site pending a federal repository; the main process building was demolished to grade in 2025 and Phase 2 decisions are pending.
operator: US Department of Energy with NYSERDA (licensee)
notes: Transuranic waste is assumed from the reprocessing history. The site also hosts closed state-licensed low-level waste trenches (halted 1975).

name: Wolf Creek Generating Station
status_note: One PWR unit in operation (operating licence 1985). Spent fuel is stored in the reactor pool(s) and in dry casks at an on-site ISFSI.

name: Yankee Rowe (ISFSI)
status_note: PWR operated 1961-1992 and was decommissioned by 2007; 15 casks of spent fuel (533 assemblies) and one cask of GTCC waste remain at the ISFSI in Rowe.

name: Zion Nuclear Power Station
status_note: Two PWR units retired in 1998 and dismantled; fuel transfer to the on-site ISFSI was completed in January 2015. The NRC released the rest of the site in November 2023, leaving the ISFSI under licence.

name: Farallon Islands radioactive waste dumping site (Pacific)
status_note: Main US Pacific dumping area west of San Francisco near the Farallon Islands: about 47,500 containers were dumped at 896-1,700 m depth between 1946 and 1970. It holds most of the activity dumped by the US in the Pacific.
notes: Lies outside the US territorial sea but within the US exclusive economic zone.

name: K-219 (sunken Soviet ballistic missile submarine)
status_note: The Yankee I-class submarine sank on 6 October 1986 north-east of Bermuda after a missile-tube explosion and fire, with its reactors and about 30 nuclear warheads on board.

name: K-278 Komsomolets (sunken Soviet nuclear submarine)
status_note: The submarine sank after a fire on 7 April 1989 and lies at 1,680 m south-west of Bear Island with its reactor (about 3 PBq remaining) and two nuclear torpedoes. Norway monitors the wreck annually; a 2019 ROV survey found intermittent releases from the reactor, suggesting damaged fuel, with little effect on the surrounding sea.
notes: The exact position is hard to fix. Lies inside Norway's exclusive economic zone but outside its territorial waters.

name: K-8 (sunken Soviet nuclear submarine, Bay of Biscay)
country: International waters (Bay of Biscay / North Atlantic)
status_note: The November-class submarine sank on 12 April 1970 after a fire, about 490 km north-west of Spain at about 4,680 m depth, with its two reactors and four nuclear torpedoes; 52 crew died during the salvage attempt.
notes: Only a rounded position (46°N 6°W) is available.

name: North-East Atlantic dumping site (46°00'N 16°45'W), used 1977-1982
status_note: Main site of the internationally coordinated North-East Atlantic dumping programme in its final years: the UK, Belgium, the Netherlands and Switzerland dumped packaged solid low-level waste here at 3,200-4,750 m depth from 1977 until dumping stopped in 1982. A moratorium followed in 1983 and dumping at sea has been banned since 1994.
notes: The site is a sea area, not a point. The IAEA describes the waste as low-level; some packages contained alpha emitters.

name: North-East Atlantic dumping site (46°15'N 17°25'W), used 1971-1976
status_note: Deep-sea site at 3,200-4,750 m used by the UK, Belgium, the Netherlands and Switzerland for packaged solid radioactive waste from 1971 to 1976, before dumping moved to the neighbouring 46°00'N 16°45'W area.

name: North-East Atlantic dumping site (48°20'N 13°16'W), used 1965-1970
status_note: Deep-sea site at 1,900-4,500 m south-west of Ireland where the UK dumped packaged radioactive waste in 1965, 1966, 1968 and 1970.
notes: Other countries may also have used this site.

name: Novaya Zemlya Trough: dumped submarine reactors (NS 421) and Kara Sea solid waste area
status_note: In 1972 reactors with spent fuel from Soviet submarine No. 421 were dumped in a metal container at about 300 m depth in the Novaya Zemlya Trough of the Kara Sea; nearby deep-water area 1 also received solid waste, including pumps from the icebreaker Lenin.
notes: Lies outside the Russian territorial sea but within the Russian exclusive economic zone.

name: Sea of Japan Soviet liquid waste dumping area 9
status_note: Area at 3,250-3,700 m depth where the Soviet Pacific Fleet discharged liquid radioactive waste; with about 401 TBq it accounts for most of the activity of the Soviet liquid waste dumped in the Pacific (1966-1992). Liquid waste disperses and is not recoverable.
notes: Centre of the dumping rectangle 41°36'-41°46'N, 133°22'-134°42'E. Other Soviet solid waste areas in the Sea of Japan are not mapped.

name: US Atlantic dumping site (38°30'N 72°06'W, '2800 m site')
status_note: The largest US Atlantic site: 14,301 containers of radioactive waste were dumped here at 1,829-2,800 m depth between 1951 and 1960. The inventory includes the reactor vessel of the submarine USS Seawolf, dumped in 1959.
notes: Activity at the time of packaging was about 2.75 PBq, mostly from the Seawolf reactor vessel (about 1.2 PBq).

name: USS Scorpion (SSN-589) wreck
status_note: The US Navy Skipjack-class nuclear submarine was lost on 22 May 1968 about 740 km south-west of the Azores with all 99 aboard; the wreck remains with its reactor and armament.
notes: Nuclear armament reportedly remains aboard.

name: USS Thresher (SSN-593) wreck
status_note: The US Navy nuclear attack submarine sank during deep-diving tests on 10 April 1963 about 350 km east of Cape Cod with all 129 aboard; the wreck and reactor remain on the seabed.

name: Koeberg Nuclear Power Station
status_note: Two PWR units (commercial 1984 and 1985) operate. The re-racked pools are nearly full, so spent fuel is also kept in dry metal casks: 15 casks were stored in the on-site Cask Storage Building (capacity 16) by late 2024, and a Transient Interim Storage Facility pad on site was due to start construction in 2025.
notes: Whether construction of the TISF began in 2025 is not confirmed.

name: Pelindaba nuclear site (Necsa) with Thabana waste area
status_note: South Africa's main nuclear research centre (SAFARI-1 reactor since 1965, former enrichment and weapons work). Its Thabana area holds waste from SAFARI-1 and part of the 1980s weapons programme: eight low-level disposal trenches dug from 1976 plus intermediate-level stores; operation ended in 1989 and a remediation strategy was being prepared in 2010.
notes: 'Closed' refers to the Thabana waste area (no new waste since 1989); the research site itself operates. The current state of remediation is unknown.

name: Vaalputs National Radioactive Waste Disposal Facility
status_note: National near-surface disposal site in the Northern Cape receiving low- and intermediate-level waste from Koeberg since October 1986, in trenches about 10 m deep. NRWDI received the nuclear installation licence (NIL-43) in July 2025 and took over operation from Necsa on 1 April 2026; a centralised interim store for Koeberg spent fuel, possibly linked to Vaalputs, is planned for 2030.
notes: The planned central interim store (CISF) may be linked to Vaalputs; its location is not fixed.
